conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:2, the seraphim covered their faces with two of their wings.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Observe the seraphim's reaction before the Lord.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: with two wings each seraph covered its face before the Lord.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Isaiah 6:2: with two wings each seraph covered its face.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See what each pair of wings was doing.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:1, tap who Isaiah saw seated on the throne.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Identify whom Isaiah sees in the vision.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah saw the Lord on the throne, in the very year the king of the land died.

feedbackWrong.b: The temple is the place the robe filled, not who was on the throne.
feedbackWrong.c: King Uzziah had died; the one on the throne in the vision is someone else.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look for who appears right after "eu vi" (I saw).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.question: According to Isaiah 6:4, what happened to the house during the vision?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Observe the effect of the voice in the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The doorposts shake at the voice, and the house fills with smoke.

feedbackWrong.a: There was a voice calling out, so loud that the doorposts moved.
feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of smoke, not light.
feedbackWrong.c: The doors shake, but the text does not say the house fell.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.b: It was filled with a bright light

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.question: Put Isaiah 6:5 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: First the cry, then the confession, and finally what he saw: the King.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "Ai de mim"; what Isaiah's eyes saw closes the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: The verse begins with a cry.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:2, how many wings did each seraph have?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the description of the seraphim.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: Six wings: two covered the face, two the feet, and two were for flying.

feedbackWrong.a: It is fewer than that: the verse describes three pairs of wings.
feedbackWrong.c: Count the pairs in the verse: face, feet, and flight. That is three pairs.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Count the pairs of wings described in the rest of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What does Isaiah 6:1 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Connect the vision of the throne to Judah's moment of crisis.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: The king of the land dies, but Isaiah sees the Lord seated on the throne.

feedbackWrong.a: In the vision the throne is occupied: the Lord is seated on it.
feedbackWrong.b: Isaiah does not take the throne; he sees who is already there.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: See who is on the throne in the year the king died.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:4–5, Isaiah feels lost because the temple was shaking and full of smoke.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Understand the cause of Isaiah's "Ai de mim".
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The text gives another reason: Isaiah is unclean, and his eyes have seen the King.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Isaiah 6:5: the reason is being a man of unclean lips and having seen the King.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See what Isaiah says after "Estou perdido!" (I am lost!).

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:5, tap the word that introduces the reason for the "Ai de mim".
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in Isaiah's confession.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" (for) opens the explanation: he is unclean and has seen the King.

feedbackWrong.a: "Então" (then) marks when Isaiah speaks, not why he speaks.
feedbackWrong.b: "Perdido" (lost) is how he feels; the reason comes right after.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look at what comes right after Isaiah's cry.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.question: How does the seraphim's gesture in Isaiah 6:2 connect to what they proclaim in 6:3?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Relate the seraphim's attitude to the holiness they proclaim.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: Those closest to the throne cover their faces and proclaim: God is holy.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of anger; they praise the Lord's holiness.
feedbackWrong.b: They stand before the Lord; Isaiah is not the center of the scene.
feedbackWrong.d: They fly above the throne; the text does not say they carry it.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Compare what they do with what they say.

options.a: They hide because God is angry with them
options.b: They cover their faces so as not to see Isaiah
options.c: Even they cover their faces before the holy God
options.d: They fly to carry God's throne across the earth

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.question: How does the scene move forward in Isaiah 6:5–6?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the confession to the seraph's coming.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah cries out, confesses his uncleanness, and then a seraph comes to him.

feedbackWrong.default: The coal arrives last, after Isaiah's cry and confession.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: The seraph moves only in the second verse.

options.a: Isaiah cries out that he is lost
options.b: Isaiah confesses his and the people's uncleanness
options.c: A seraph comes to him with a coal

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:4, what did the doorposts do at the voice that called out?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Understand the effect of the proclaimed holiness on the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The voice proclaiming holiness makes even the temple's structure shake.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of doors opening; it speaks of the doorposts shaking.
feedbackWrong.c: Nothing closes in the text; the doorposts shake at the voice.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Think of the effect of a very loud voice on a building.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What links Isaiah 6:3 to Revelation 4:8?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Relate Isaiah's vision to the worship in Revelation.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: In Isaiah and in Revelation, six-winged beings repeat: "Santo, santo, santo".

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text shows a plea for forgiveness; both show praise.
feedbackWrong.c: The praise does not change: centuries later, the same "Santo, santo, santo" goes on.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: Compare what the six-winged beings say in the two texts.

options.a: The same cry before the throne

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:5, Isaiah counts himself among an unclean people instead of thinking he is better than others.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Interpret Isaiah's confession as humility before the holy God.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: Before the holy God, Isaiah compares himself to no one: he and the people need God.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Isaiah 6:5: he says he lives among a people of unclean lips, like himself.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See where Isaiah says he lives.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:3, tap the phrase that shows God's glory is not confined to the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the holy God's glory fills the world.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: The vision happens in the temple, but the holy God's glory fills the whole world.

feedbackWrong.b: "Dos Exércitos" (of hosts) speaks of the Lord's power, not the reach of his glory.
feedbackWrong.c: "Uns aos outros" (to one another) shows how the seraphim proclaim, not how far the glory goes.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look in the second half of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.question: What reading does Isaiah 6:2–3 support about God's holiness?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God's holiness.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The seraphim cover their faces and say "santo" three times: God is unlike anything.

feedbackWrong.b: If it were only kindness, the seraphim would not cover their faces before him.
feedbackWrong.c: They cover their faces and proclaim another's holiness: only the Lord is called holy.
feedbackWrong.d: The cry itself says the whole earth is full of his glory.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Compare each option with what the seraphim do and say.

options.a: God is unlike anything, and even the seraphim cover themselves
options.b: Holy just means God is very nice
options.c: The seraphim are almost equal to the Lord
options.d: God is holy only in heaven; the earth is left out

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.question: Which sequence shows the thread of "Santo, santo, santo" in the Bible?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.learningObjective: See Isaiah 6:3 as the start of a thread that runs through the Bible.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah's vision points to Jesus and goes on in praise that never stops.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: Isaiah (Isa 6:3), the Gospel of John (John 12:41), and Revelation (Rev 4:8).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: Start with the prophet and end with the vision at the close of the Bible.

options.a: Isaiah sees the throne and hears the seraphim proclaim holiness
options.b: John says Isaiah saw Jesus' glory
options.c: Before the throne, the holy cry does not stop day or night

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:1, what is the Lord seated on?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God's reign in the scene.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The king of the land died, but the Lord still reigns: he is in his place as King.

feedbackWrong.b: The altar appears in Isaiah 6:6; here it is the place from which the Lord reigns.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of a mountain; it speaks of where the King sits.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Think of the place from which a king rules.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What links Isaiah 6:3 to 1 Peter 1:15–16?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Connect God's holiness in Isaiah to the call of his people in the NT.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: The God the seraphim call holy calls his people to be holy too.

feedbackWrong.b: Peter asks for holiness "in all your conduct", not only in the temple.
feedbackWrong.c: Peter speaks to those called by God, not to angels.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: See why Peter says the people must be holy.

options.a: The Holy One calls us to be holy
options.b: Holiness is only for the temple
options.c: Only angels need to be holy

estudo:entrada-deus-03.context: Uzziah reigned over Judah for many years, and his death left the people insecure. That same year, the prophet Isaiah is in the temple and receives a vision: he sees who is truly on the throne.
estudo:entrada-deus-03.focusQuestion: How does God's holiness change the way you come near to him?
estudo:entrada-deus-03.keywordGloss: Set apart, pure, and unlike anything that exists; said three times, it marks what God is to the highest degree.
facts: Isaiah saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne.
The seraphim proclaimed that the Lord is holy, holy, holy.
The whole earth is full of God's glory.
The house was filled with smoke.
Isaiah admits he is a man of unclean lips.
